Theory revision: Theorem 1's upper bound is not just a transport-cost bound, it's a PERCEPTUAL-QUALITY bound. Sinkhorn OOM root cause identified as ARCHITECTURE flaw, not parameter issue. Three flaws: (1) triple-nested Python loop (8 regions × 24 batch × 64 projections = 12288 Sinkhorn calls); (2) each call built full autograd graph through n_iters iterations → 122880 intermediate tensors; (3) projection cap (min(P,16)) was a parameter-level hack. Architecture fix applied: (A) _sinkhorn_1d_batched replaces _sinkhorn_1d — envelope theorem (detached dual variables f,g under no_grad; gradient flows only through cost matrix C=(a-b)^2 in final <T*,C>) eliminates n_iters× autograd depth; (B) projection vectorization — all P projections processed in parallel via batched [P,N,M] tensors, eliminating innermost for-p loop; (C) removed projection cap hack. Standard OT library practice (POT, geomloss use same envelope theorem principle).

Sinkhorn training started (job-d2b24f18). Config: ε=0.1, iters=10, P=16, batch=12 (VRAM budget on 8GB RTX 4070: [P,N,M] cost matrix retained for backward limits P to 16). First 26 iters: 1.40 s/it, tswd=1.3887, loss=19.52, VRAM 7.0GB/8.2GB (88% util). Architecture fix confirmed working — no OOM, full P=16 + batch=12 stable. ETA ~50min for 5 epochs.

Soft OOM detected (job-d2b24f18): speed degraded from 1.4 s/it to 18-24 s/it at iteration 180+. Process didn't crash (no CUDA OOM error) but became unusably slow due to PyTorch caching allocator pressure. Root cause: even with detached duals, the [P,N,M] cost matrix C in _sinkhorn_1d_batched is retained for backward across all 8*12=96 loop iterations simultaneously in the autograd graph (96 * [16, ~256, ~256] * 4B ≈ 1.5GB+ of retained intermediates). This is a deeper architecture issue than the envelope theorem fix addressed.

Second architecture fix applied: gradient checkpointing via torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint. Each _sinkhorn_1d_batched call is now wrapped in checkpoint(use_reentrant=False): forward computes cost matrix C=[P,N,M] and discards it (only scalar result retained); backward recomputes C on demand. This caps autograd memory at O(1 simultaneously-live cost matrix) instead of O(96). Tradeoff: ~1.8x compute overhead (2.34 s/it vs 1.4 s/it) but ELIMINATES soft OOM. Results: VRAM 7.0GB→4.8GB (-31%), speed stable at 2.34 s/it through 211+ iterations (previous run degraded at iter 180). tswd converging normally: 1.61→1.34→1.20→1.14. ETA ~81min for 5 epochs.

Third architecture fix: chunked checkpoint with empty_cache. The checkpoint-only fix still had soft OOM at iter 97 (32 s/it). Root cause: 96 scalar cost nodes + their gp/tp leaf tensors retained simultaneously cause PyTorch caching allocator FRAGMENTATION (not raw memory exhaustion). Fix: process 96 calls in CHUNKS of 8, del chunk_pairs + torch.cuda.empty_cache() between chunks. This releases gp/tp leaf tensor references, letting the allocator defrag. Results: VRAM 4.8GB→2.64GB (-45%), speed 2.10 s/it stable through 195+ iters. The returned total_cost retains autograd connection (no manual backward) so outer loss.backward() works correctly.

Mechanism 5 (Spectral-decoupled region SWD) implemented: _semantic_region_swd_spectral. Architecture change: DWT-decompose gen/target into LL (low-freq) and LH/HL/HH (high-freq). LL gets GLOBAL SWD (K=1, preserve structure). LH/HL/HH get REGION SWD (K=8, match texture per content region). Theoretical motivation: style (brushstrokes) is high-freq, content (structure) is low-freq. A single spatial partition conflates them; frequency-band division lets each band use its optimal K. This is a deeper change than the 4 mechanisms: it changes WHERE SWD operates (frequency domain) rather than HOW region partitioning works. Integrates with existing DWT route architecture. Config: sem_r8_spectral.json (ll_weight=1.0, hf_weight=2.0 up-weights texture).

Mechanism 6 (Attention-guided style-conditional region SWD) implemented: _semantic_region_swd_attn. Architecture change: replace k-means region definition (content-based, style-AGNOSTIC) with cross-attention map (style-CONDITIONAL). Same content point belongs to different regions for different target styles. Uses hard top-k membership (lesson from soft-mask MUSIQ crash: hard boundaries preserve sharpness). Theoretical motivation: a 'sky' region should be matched differently to Impressionism (brushstroke sky) vs Ukiyo-e (flat color sky). This is a deeper change: it replaces the region DEFINITION (content k-means → attention map) rather than the region MATCHING. Config: sem_r8_attn.json.
